sections.section_name: Section A - Choose the Correct Answer

questions.question_text: What should your eyes follow closely when trying to catch a ball?
options: A) The ground
B) The movement of the ball
C) The sky
D) Your teammates' shoes
questions.answer: B) The movement of the ball

questions.question_text: Which part of your foot is best for passing a football accurately to a short distance?
options: A) The toe
B) The heel
C) The inside of the foot
D) The bottom sole
questions.answer: C) The inside of the foot

questions.question_text: When performing an overhand throw, where should you step?
options: A) Step backward away from the target
B) Step sideways with both feet
C) Step forward with the foot opposite to your throwing arm
D) Keep both feet firmly glued to the ground
questions.answer: C) Step forward with the foot opposite to your throwing arm

questions.question_text: What is the correct grip used for striking a shuttlecock with a racket?
options: A) A tight fist grip
B) A relaxed handshake grip
C) Holding it by the strings
D) Pinching it with two fingers

questions.question_text: How should your hands be positioned to catch a ball coming towards your chest?
options: A) Fingers pointing down to the ground
B) Hands in your pockets
C) Fingers pointing up with thumbs together forming a W or triangle
D) Arms crossed over the chest
questions.answer: C) Fingers pointing up with thumbs together forming a W or triangle

questions.question_text: When running or doing 'Little Steps', how should your elbows be positioned?
options: A) Completely straight and stiff
B) Bent at a right angle and moving forward and back
C) Flapping out to the sides like bird wings
D) Held tightly against the stomach
questions.answer: B) Bent at a right angle and moving forward and back

questions.question_text: What happens when you 'cushion' a ball while receiving a pass in soccer?
options: A) You kick it as hard as possible
B) You let it bounce away from you
C) You pull your foot back slightly on impact to absorb the ball's energy
D) You step on top of it with all your body weight
questions.answer: C) You pull your foot back slightly on impact to absorb the ball's energy

questions.question_text: When striking a shuttlecock in an underhand serve, where must the racket hit the shuttlecock?
options: A) Above your head
B) At chest level
C) Below your waist
D) At shoulder height

questions.question_text: What is the main purpose of practicing 'Little Steps' drills?
options: A) To improve footwork, agility, and balance
B) To practice sleeping positions
C) To stretch the back muscles
D) To rest during a game
questions.answer: A) To improve footwork, agility, and balance

questions.question_text: Which action shows good follow-through after throwing a ball?
options: A) Stopping your arm immediately after the ball leaves your hand
B) Letting your throwing arm continue its motion pointing toward the target
C) Turning around and walking away
D) Dropping your arm straight down to your side instantly
questions.answer: B) Letting your throwing arm continue its motion pointing toward the target

questions.question_text: Describe the correct basic stance to prepare for catching a ball. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, bend your knees slightly, keep your eyes focused on the ball, and hold your hands ready out in front.

questions.question_text: Which part of the shoe should you use to kick a ball with maximum power, and why? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: To kick with maximum power, you should lock your ankle and strike the ball using the top part, or laces, of your shoe for a strong impact.

questions.question_text: Why is it important to have 'soft hands' when catching a fast ball? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Having soft hands means pulling your arms slightly toward your chest as the ball hits them. This absorbs the impact and stops the ball from bouncing out.

questions.question_text: State two things you should keep in mind while taking 'little steps' or jogging in place. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: You should stay light on the balls of your feet and keep your arms pumping rhythmically to maintain good balance and speed.

questions.question_text: How do you correctly track a shuttlecock coming toward you before striking it? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Move your feet quickly to get your body directly behind or slightly beneath the falling shuttlecock while keeping your eyes fixed on its cork base.

questions.question_text: Imagine you are getting ready to serve a shuttlecock in a game. Describe your stance and how you strike it over the net. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: I stand behind the line with my non-racket foot forward. I hold the shuttlecock gently by the feathers and drop it. As it falls below my waist, I swing my racket underhand and flick my wrist to hit the cork smoothly over the net.

questions.question_text: Imagine you are dribbling a soccer ball past an opponent. Describe your movements and how you keep control of the ball. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: I lean slightly forward, keeping the ball very close to my toes. I use quick, light touches with the inside and outside of my shoes to guide the ball forward, keeping my head up to watch the opponent while protecting it.

questions.question_text: Explain the correct sequence of actions for passing a ball accurately to a teammate who is running ahead of you. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: First, look to see where your teammate is running, not just where they are standing. Step forward with your opposite foot to build momentum. Push the ball out into the empty space in front of them so they can catch it without slowing down, letting your throwing arm follow through toward the target.

questions.question_text: How does using your arms properly help you run faster and maintain balance during a sprint? [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Proper arm swings create a strong rhythm and push your body forward. You should bend your elbows at a right angle and swing them back and forth from your pockets up to your chin. This strong pumping action balances your fast leg movements and stops your upper body from twisting side to side.
